hook.speaker: King Brihadratha
hook.setting: The king's plea after listing everything that passes.
hook.sanskrit: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
hook.line: Like a frog in a dark well, I am stuck in this life. Show me the way out.
hook.translation: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
hook.why: Even success can leave you feeling stuck; asking for help is the first step out.

verse.speaker: Sanatkumara
verse.setting: The next step: action rests on happiness.
verse.sanskrit: यदा वै सुखं लभतेऽथ करोति नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति सुखमेव लब्ध्वा करोति सुखं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमिति सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verse.line: We act only when we find joy in it. Understand the joy, and action follows.
verse.translation: When one finds happiness, one acts. No one acts without finding happiness; only by finding happiness does one act. So happiness itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand happiness.'
verse.why: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

prasang.title: Narada: learned but sad
prasang.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasang.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.
prasang.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

why: We act only when we find joy; find where the joy is.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
verse.line: Devoted to your own work, you reach fulfilment. Here's how.
verse.translation: Each person, devoted to his own work, attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to his own work finds perfection.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

why: Enjoying what arrives unplanned

story.title: Sampati's burned wings
story.story_hook: The monkeys had given up and were waiting to die when a vulture with no wings spoke to them.
story.summary: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.
story.lesson: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.
story.hook_title: The monkeys had given up and sat down to die, until an old vulture spoke
story.teaser: The monkeys had given up and sat down to die, until an old vulture spoke

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verse.sanskrit: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
verse.line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.

verse.setting: Narada to Shuka on why more is never enough.
verse.sanskrit: अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम् / तस्मात्संतोषमेवेह धनं पश्यन्ति पण्डिताः
verse.line: There's no end to wanting. Contentment is the highest happiness, and the real wealth.

verse.setting: How a householder becomes a 'world' for others.

verse.line: Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
verse.translation: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.

why: Become a world for others.

verse.line: Give me something to hold on to, so I can get through these years.
verse.translation: Now, gracious one, whatever you command I will do, holding it on my head with respect. But give me something to lean on, Lord, something I can serve, so that I can get through these years.

story.title: Manki's song: desire, I know your root
story.story_hook: Manki put every coin he had into two young oxen, and lost both in a single afternoon.
story.summary: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
story.lesson: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
story.teaser: Manki put every coin he had into two young oxen, and lost both in a single afternoon.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Young Rama, back from his travels, tells the sages in his father's court why nothing interests him.
verse.sanskrit: किं मे राज्येन किं भोगैः कोऽहं किमिदमागतम् । यन्मिथ्यैवास्तु तन्मिथ्या कस्य नाम किमागतम् ॥
verse.line: What is a kingdom to me, or pleasure? Who am I, and what is all this for?
verse.translation: What is kingship to me, and what are pleasures? Who am I, and what is all this that has come to me? If it is unreal, let it be unreal; whose is it, and what has anyone gained?
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
verse.misuse: Rama's question opens the teaching; it isn't the answer. Follow it with 6a.115.43 or 1.30.17.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
verse.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
verse.translation: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verse.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

why: The river called Hope (Bhartrihari, Vairagya Shataka 10)

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
verse.line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.
verse.translation: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.speaker: Sanatkumara
verse.sanskrit: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verse.line: Happiness is in the vast. There is no happiness in the small.
verse.translation: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
verse.why: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

prasang.title: Narada: learned but sad
prasang.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasang.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.
prasang.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

why: the small always leaves a thirst for more; the wanting is for the vast
We act only when we find joy; find where the joy is.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥
verse.line: Money goes one of three ways: given, enjoyed, or lost. Neither give nor enjoy it, and it is lost.
verse.translation: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
verse.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

why: Give

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha's closing advice to Rama on living in the world after the three vows.
verse.sanskrit: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥
verse.line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
verse.translation: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

why: an inner anchor during activity

story.title: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf
story.story_hook: The whole world was one dark ocean, and on it floated a single banyan tree with a child asleep on a branch.
story.summary: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
story.lesson: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
story.hook_title: An old sage drifted alone over a drowned world, and found a child asleep on a leaf
story.teaser: An old sage drifted alone over a drowned world, and found a child asleep on a leaf
